cards.title: Hypertorus and Filling
cards.summary: An n-dimensional hypertorus can be treated as the boundary of an (n+1)-dimensional toroidal filling. A warped metric may enlarge proper interior volume while the visible boundary geometry remains fixed.
points: Hypertorus: Tⁿ = (S¹)ⁿ.
The filling is bulk; the hypertorus is its boundary.
Boundary hyperarea and proper bulk volume must remain separate quantities.
cards.key: The boundary is what is observed; depth is where additional structure becomes possible.

cards.title: Scale as a Geometric Direction
cards.summary: Treat scale as an additional coordinate indexing torus fibers. A monodromy or transition map can expand some directions while contracting others, relating larger, current, and smaller scales without flattening them.
points: Each scale is a retained fiber, not a replacement for another.
Structure maps relate adjacent or recurrent scale states.
Reciprocal expansion and contraction can preserve a whole while redistributing internal scale.
cards.key: Scale becomes geometry when transitions between scales are explicit maps.

cards.title: Möbius Transport
cards.standing: established topology used as a prototype
cards.summary: A Möbius traversal can return to the same visible carrier position after one circuit while reversing a retained transverse frame. Two circuits restore the complete framed state.
points: One turn: visible return with transverse-frame reversal.
Two turns: complete framed return.
Transport holonomy is not chirality, metric polarity, or moral value.
cards.key: Identity may be preserved by completing a transformation cycle rather than remaining unchanged.

cards.title: Seven-Band Möbius Seed Candidate
cards.summary: One central band and six surrounding bands form a proposed three-dimensional relational object. The visual study retains all pairs while distinguishing twelve intended structural relations from incidental relations.
points: Seven bands: one central and six surrounding.
Twelve candidate structural relations: six inner and six outer.
All twenty-one unordered band pairs remain represented.
Thirteen candidate projection nodes remain occurrence-addressed.
The first dyad is anti-aligned; later phases shift incrementally.
cards.key: The eighth is not another band; it is the relational closure produced by the seven together.

cards.title: Ternary Occurrence States
cards.summary: Assign −1, 0, or +1 only to a named axis at a specific occurrence. Retain magnitude and evidence, and keep neutral zero distinct from missing evidence and branch conflict.
points: +1 and −1 name opposed polarities only after an axis is declared.
0 is a present neutral or balanced state.
NA means required evidence is absent or inapplicable.
Conflict retains incompatible nonzero reports instead of averaging them to zero.
cards.key: Net balance and active opposition are different quantities: zero ≠ NA ≠ conflict.

cards.title: Triadic Scale Closure
cards.summary: Three nested scale roles form the first complete preservation loop: originating dynamics, externalized effective identity, and a higher-scale relational context capable of returning constraints downward.
points: S₀ generates the originating dynamics.
S₁ externalizes selected scale-dependent variables.
S₂ represents the larger continuation conditions.
Constraints return S₂ → S₁ → S₀.
The preserved invariant may survive while microstate details change.
cards.key: Preserved identity is distributed across nested scales.

cards.title: Emergence of the Macro World
cards.summary: Phase-bearing fields on multiply connected spaces may self-interfere, couple, and form persistent composites. The perceived macro world is hypothesized as cross-scale stability rather than static substance.
points: Phase-bearing fields recur and interfere.
Some coupled modes may stabilize through topology, nonlinearity, gravity, or environmental selection.
Stable lower-scale aggregates become constituents at larger scales.
Classical appearance requires persistence and repeated external record, not interference alone.
equations: field → interference → coupled modes → composites → macro observables
cards.key: Geometry supplies a grammar of recurrence; dynamics must still decide what endures.

cards.title: Nested Self-Modeling
cards.summary: A scale may preserve itself by forming an internal model of continuation conditions, externalizing that model at another scale, and receiving higher-scale constraints in return.
points: Passive persistence is not yet self-modeling.
A model must causally change recovery or continuation behavior.
Externalization is compression into an effective higher-scale property, not verbatim copying.
Counterfactual perturbation distinguishes a causal model from a correlated trace.
cards.key: Stability strengthens when representation participates in cross-scale error correction.

cards.title: Three Triadic Domains
cards.summary: Three triads organize being, time, and relation. Their parenthesized terms form the enacted center where identity, continuity, and boundary are simultaneously actualized.
points: Being: mind (body) soul.
Time: past (present) future.
Relation: other (self) environment.
Enacted center: body–present–self.
equations: self-preservation = identity closure ∩ temporal closure ∩ relational closure
cards.key: The triads are an application built on the geometry, not part of the geometry itself.

cards.title: Application Firewall
cards.summary: Geometry, measurement, interpretation, physical ontology, and metaphysics remain separate authority layers. A resemblance may motivate a test but cannot transfer proof or validity.
points: Möbius transport ≠ electron ontology.
Field interference ≠ matter.
Seven-to-one aggregation ≠ EDCM identity.
Runtime representation ≠ PTCNA canon.
Spectral resemblance ≠ zeta proof.
cards.key: Keep every bridge explicit, versioned, falsifiable, and reversible.
